rounds.proof_sketch: N=4096, BLOCK_SIZE=16. Loop k iterates 0,16,32,...,4080. tx∈[0,15]. Original condition: k+tx ∈ [0,4095], always <4096. Mutated condition: k-tx ∈ [-15,4080], always <4096. Both predicates are ALWAYS TRUE for this fixed N that is perfectly divisible by BLOCK_SIZE.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the bounds-check condition from (k+tx)<N to (k-tx)<N when loading tile_A. However, for N=4096 and BLOCK_SIZE=16, the matrix dimensions are perfectly divisible by the tile size. The loop iterates k from 0 to 4080 in steps of 16. At the maximum k=4080 with maximum tx=15, the original condition evaluates 4095<4096 (TRUE). The mutated condition evaluates 4065<4096 (TRUE). Since both conditions are always satisfied for all valid (k,tx) combinations, the else branch (setting tile_A to 0.0f) is never executed in either version. The actual memory access A[row*N+(k+tx)] remains unchanged. Therefore, both kernels produce identical results for any input values.
rounds.kill_strategy: Cannot kill - the mutation changes a bounds-check predicate that is always TRUE for the fixed shape N=4096. The mutant would only behave differently if N were not a multiple of BLOCK_SIZE=16, but changing N requires changing the tensor shape which is forbidden.
rounds.recommendations: When designing tiled CUDA kernels, consider testing with matrix dimensions that are NOT exact multiples of the tile/block size to ensure boundary conditions are properly exercised. For mutation testing coverage, varying the compile-time constants (like BLOCK_SIZE) or testing with non-aligned dimensions would catch predicate mutations in bounds-checking code.
